edges.description: Mutant MSL3 loses its interactions with MOF and MSL1, so the MSL complex does not assemble normally.
Without an intact MSL complex, MOF-dependent H4K16 acetylation falls.
Reduced H4K16ac is accompanied by transcriptome changes, mainly downregulation, of genes in developmental pathways.
Patient fibroblasts migrate faster than controls, a cellular readout of the cell-migration pathway changes.
The neurodevelopmental intermediates between reduced H4K16ac-dependent transcription and developmental delay are not characterised in human neural tissue.
Intellectual disability follows from the same uncharacterised neurodevelopmental intermediates.
How MSL complex dysfunction produces hypoplasia of the inferior cerebellar vermis has not been studied.
Infantile truncal hypotonia is a near-constant feature; its mechanism downstream of MSL3 loss is uncharacterised.
Autism spectrum disorder affects about half of assessed individuals; the neural intermediates are uncharacterised.

nodes.description: MSL3 patient-derived fibroblasts migrate faster than control fibroblasts in vitro, and HDAC inhibitor treatment restores control-like migratory behaviour. This is a cellular readout in peripheral cells, not a demonstrated cause of any clinical phenotype.

evidence.snippet: Twenty-two of 25 (88%) individuals had a history of abnormal muscle tone, comprising truncal muscular hypotonia (n = 21) and/or spasticity of the upper and lower limbs (n = 7) while 5 individuals had mixed tone.

nodes.description: Patient-derived cells show global transcriptome alterations, predominantly downregulation, of genes in morphogenesis and cell-migration pathways. HDAC inhibitor treatment rescues selected downregulated targets. The steps linking these changes in peripheral cells to brain and other organ phenotypes have not been shown in human neural tissue, so the edges from this node to clinical phenotypes are recorded as indirect.

evidence.reference_title: Defining the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of X-linked MSL3-related disorder.
evidence.snippet: Transcriptome analyses of patient cells showed dysregulation, mainly downregulation, of genes involved in developmental pathways.

nodes.description: Developmental delay is present in all reported cohort individuals, global in 24 of 25 and isolated speech delay in one, and is evident from infancy.

evidence.snippet: Developmental delay (DD) was prominent in all individuals (n = 25/25, 100%), with global DD in 24/25 (96%) individuals and isolated speech development delay in 1/25 (4%) individual.

nodes.description: Growth hormone deficiency was reported in one boy in a two-patient Chinese case report, who responded to recombinant growth hormone. Its frequency in the disorder is unknown.

evidence.snippet: Four novel phenotypic characteristics of MRXSBA individuals were identified, including growth hormone deficiency (GHD), slow growth of permanent teeth, scoliosis, and cleft palate.

nodes.description: In patient-derived cells, HDAC inhibitors restored H4K16ac, rescued selected downregulated genes and normalised fibroblast migration. This has not been tested in patients and is recorded as a mechanism-directed experimental lead, not a clinical therapy.

evidence.snippet: All variants were located within the last eight exons (exon 6–13) of MSL3 (NM_078629.4), encoding the MRG domain, whereas no variants were detected within the first six exons.

nodes.description: Pathogenic MSL3 alleles are predominantly loss-of-function (nonsense, frameshift, splice-site and multi-exon deletion), with a minority of missense and in-frame variants at conserved MRG-domain residues. All reported causative variants lie in exons 6-13, which encode the MRG domain; the cohort authors suggest that a shorter transcript may compensate for truncating variants in the first exons, a hypothesis that has not been tested experimentally.

evidence.reference_title: Defining the genotypic and phenotypic spectrum of X-linked MSL3-related disorder.
evidence.snippet: We identified multiple variant types in MSL3 (ten nonsense, six frameshift, four splice site, three missense, one in-frame-deletion, one multi-exon deletion), most proven to be de novo, and clustering in the terminal eight exons suggesting that truncating variants in the first five exons might be compensated by an alternative MSL3 transcript.

evidence.reference_title: Two Chinese patients with Basilicata-Akhtar syndrome caused by novel MSL3 variants: a case report and literature review.
evidence.snippet: Our data support the notion that the MRG domain of MSL3 is intolerant to loss-of-function variants and responsible for MSL3 function.

nodes.description: In one boy with growth hormone deficiency, recombinant human growth hormone improved height over more than 10 years of follow-up without reported adverse effects. This is single-patient evidence and applies only to individuals with documented growth hormone deficiency.
